title: Self-Privilege Escalation via employees/{empId} Self-Update Denylist
code_evidence: match /employees/{empId} allow update uses a denylist (!affectedKeys().hasAny([...])) that omits explicitAttendanceDelegation, delegatedEmployeeIds, delegatedBranchIds, authorizedBranchIds, authorizedDepartmentIds, authorizedTeamIds, managerId, and supervisorId. ServerAttendanceService.resolveTrustedActor reads these exact fields from empData (lines 251, 269, 272, 275, 278, 281).
security_impact: Any authenticated EMPLOYEE, HEAD_TELLER, SUPERVISOR, or MANAGER can directly update their own employees/{empId} document via Firestore client SDK to grant themselves explicitAttendanceDelegation=true, delegatedEmployeeIds, or tenant-wide authorizedBranchIds/authorizedDepartmentIds, escalating privileges in /api/attendance/*.
required_correction: Switch employees/{empId} self-update to a strict allowlist (contact/profile fields only), or add all delegation and scope fields to the denylist AND read delegation/scope exclusively from server-protected fields.

title: Self-Service Tampering & Optional Audit Attribution on Direct Firestore Writes
code_evidence: canWriteAttendanceForEmployee makes recordedBy, actorId, and performedBy optional (!('recordedBy' in data) || ...). Furthermore, allow update on attendance_logs, attendance_records, attendance_sessions, and attendance only calls canWriteAttendanceForEmployee(...) without restricting self-service updates.
security_impact: Any self-target (EMPLOYEE, JUNIOR_TELLER, SENIOR_TELLER) can use the Firestore client SDK directly to overwrite their own checkIn, checkOut, realHours, variance, status, or overrideReason on existing attendance records, and omit recordedBy/actorId completely.
required_correction: Block client-side allow update on attendance_logs/attendance_records/attendance (route corrections through server API or restrict update to OWNER/MANAGER) and require recordedBy == request.auth.uid && actorId == request.auth.uid on all creates/updates.

title: Dual-Field getBusinessId(data) Allows Conflicting businessId vs business_id
code_evidence: getBusinessId(data) checks data.get('businessId', data.get('business_id', ...)) with camelCase taking precedence, without enforcing equality when both keys exist in the same document.
security_impact: A client can write a document containing businessId='biz_actor' (passing Firestore rules) alongside business_id='biz_victim', poisoning snake_case tenant queries, audit trails, and payroll aggregations.
required_correction: Enforce (!('businessId' in data) || !('business_id' in data) || data.businessId == data.business_id) and require canonical business_id presence in getBusinessId / attendance write rules.

title: Missing Payroll Period Lock Enforcement in Firestore Security Rules
code_evidence: No attendance match block (attendance_logs, attendance_records, attendance_sessions, attendance_status, attendance_adjustment_requests) checks whether the target date falls inside a LOCKED/SEALED/PAID payroll_cycles document.
security_impact: Direct Firestore client writes (including offline fallback or direct SDK calls) bypass payroll period lock if the client omits AttendanceRepository.verifyPeriodLock.
required_correction: Disable or restrict direct client mutations on attendance_logs/attendance_records/attendance_sessions/attendance_status for locked periods, or route all attendance mutations exclusively through Admin SDK endpoints.

line_refs: Multiple Direct-Firestore Attendance Write Paths Bypass /api/attendance/* & AttendanceAuthorizationService
title: AttendanceLedger.tsx overrides (765, 811), recalculations (854), deletions (906), and DD/MM/YYYY auto-repair (178-180); MyWorkspace.tsx clock-in/out (440, 461); MassImportModal.tsx confirmImport (542); EmployeeRepository.saveAttendanceLog (702); and AttendanceRepository.createAdjustmentRequest/approveAdjustmentRequest/updateRecord/saveRecord/batchSaveRecords/batchDeleteRecords all write directly to Firestore client SDK.
code_evidence: All these workflows skip ServerAttendanceService, server-side badge checks, server audit_logs writes, and in several cases skip AttendanceAuthorizationService, verifyPeriodLock, or dual attendance_logs+attendance_records+attendance_sessions synchronization.
verification_status: Route overrides, adjustments, bulk imports, and MyWorkspace clock-in/out through server Admin endpoints (/api/attendance/*) or enforce full server-side RBAC + period-lock + audit guarantees.

title: HEAD_TELLER Empty-Branch Delegation Grants Tenant-Wide Authority & Rules/Server Divergence
code_evidence: In hasExplicitTellerDelegation, if actor.explicitAttendanceDelegation === true and actorBranches.size === 0 (and no delegatedBranchIds), line 355 returns (actorBranches.size === 0) => true, allowing attendance across ALL branches. Additionally, firestore.rules only checks explicitAttendanceDelegation + branchId and ignores delegatedEmployeeIds/delegatedBranchIds/permissions.
security_impact: A delegated HEAD_TELLER lacking a branchId field gets tenant-wide attendance write access across all branches on the server, while delegatedEmployeeIds/delegatedBranchIds behave inconsistently between server API and Firestore rules.
required_correction: Fail closed when actorBranches.size === 0 unless delegatedEmployeeIds or delegatedBranchIds explicitly authorizes the target; align Firestore rules and ServerAttendanceService delegation structures.

title: QR Badge Signature Verification Bypassed When Signature or Badge Fields Are Omitted
code_evidence: verifyScannedBadgeSecurity wraps cryptographic comparison in if (signature) { ... } (line 158), returning { valid: true } when an unsigned QR string is scanned for an ACTIVE badge. On the server, verifyBadgeIfProvided returns early at line 393 if badgeId, qrSignature, and badgePayload are all omitted even when method === 'QR'. Line 452 falls back to docs[0] without rejecting duplicate active badges.
security_impact: Client kiosk accepts forged plain-ID QR scans lacking a signature even for employees with active signed badges; direct callers to POST /api/attendance/check-in with method='QR' can omit badge fields entirely to skip badge status/expiry/signature verification.
required_correction: Require a valid cryptographic signature whenever an ACTIVE badge exists (on client) and require badgeId+qrSignature whenever method === 'QR' or 'NFC' (on server); reject ambiguous duplicate active badge records.

title: Adjustment Request Approval Lacks Maker-Checker Separation, RBAC Enforcement, and Canonical business_id
code_evidence: createAdjustmentRequest writes only businessId (no business_id) and skips verifyPeriodLock. approveAdjustmentRequest performs no AttendanceAuthorizationService RBAC check, does not enforce actor.id !== request.requestedBy (Maker-Checker), skips verifyPeriodLock if session doc is missing, and omits attendance_records update. In firestore.rules:1351-1356, SUPERVISOR can self-approve adjustment requests.
security_impact: An employee or supervisor can request an hours adjustment and an unauthorized actor or the requester themselves (Maker=Checker) can approve it, altering attendance_sessions and attendance_logs (even during locked payroll periods if session doc is absent) without updating attendance_records.
required_correction: Move adjustment request creation/approval to server API with strict Maker-Checker enforcement (approver !== requester), OWNER/MANAGER-only approval, mandatory verifyPeriodLock, canonical business_id, and synchronized attendance_records updates.

title: audit_logs Written Outside Firestore Transaction and Errors Silently Swallowed
code_evidence: recordAuditEvent executes outside adminDb.runTransaction and wraps adminDb.collection('audit_logs').doc(...).set(...) in try/catch { console.warn(...) }.
security_impact: An attendance check-in, check-out, or override can commit permanently to attendance_status, attendance_sessions, attendance_logs, attendance_records, and attendance_events while its forensic audit_logs record silently fails to persist.
required_correction: Include audit_logs doc creation inside adminDb.runTransaction for checkInWithAdmin, checkOutWithAdmin, and overrideAttendanceWithAdmin so state mutation and forensic audit log are strictly atomic.

title: Payroll Period Lock Read Outside Transaction & Single-Field business_id Query
code_evidence: verifyPayrollPeriodUnlocked executes before adminDb.runTransaction (TOCTOU window) and queries only .where('business_id', '==', canonicalBusinessId) (same in client AttendanceRepository.verifyPeriodLock, plus 30s cache). Legacy payroll_cycles docs using camelCase businessId are missed.
security_impact: 1) A concurrent payroll cycle lock can complete between verifyPayrollPeriodUnlocked and transaction commit. 2) Any payroll_cycles document lacking snake_case business_id is silently ignored by period lock enforcement. 3) Client 30s cache can lag behind newly locked cycles.
required_correction: Re-verify payroll lock status inside adminDb.runTransaction (or enforce cycle lock documents) and support canonical/camelCase parity validation during cycle reads.

title: Stale Multi-Day Active Session Overwrite, Non-Transactional Session Lookup, & Missing Idempotency Key
code_evidence: checkInWithAdmin only blocks duplicate check-in when prevDate === dateStr (lines 768-778); if prior day was never closed, it overwrites attendance_status.activeSessionId, stranding the prior session in status='ACTIVE'. checkOutWithAdmin resolves activeSessionId/session outside transaction and unconditionally sets activeSessionId: null without checking activeSessionId == sessionId. No idempotencyKey exists.
security_impact: 1) Unclosed previous-day sessions become orphaned ACTIVE records invisible to attendance_status. 2) Concurrent check-in + check-out races can null out a newer session's activeSessionId. 3) Network retries on check-in create duplicate attempts returning 409 instead of idempotent replay.
required_correction: Require explicit session reconciliation or flagging for prior-day ACTIVE sessions, verify activeSessionId === sessionId inside checkOutWithAdmin transaction before clearing, and support client idempotency keys.

title: Direct Firestore Fallback Leaks When !apiResp?.session, Offline Sync Hardcodes EMPLOYEE Actor, & Client Trust Flaws
code_evidence: 1) AttendanceRepository checkIn/checkOut calls safeFetchJson, which throws on HTTP 4xx/5xx, but if a proxy returns 200 without .session (line 293/578), it silently falls through to direct Firestore. 2) Direct fallback never verifies badge signature/status/expiry. 3) offlineSync.ts:74 hardcodes actor={id: record.employeeId, name:'Offline Sync', role:'EMPLOYEE'} and branchId='UNKNOWN', failing OWNER-queued third-party scans and impersonating employee if unauthenticated. 4) AttendanceStatus.update in firestore.rules:1438-1440 allows employeeId mutation if legacy resource lacked employeeId.
security_impact: Offline/fallback paths have inconsistent RBAC, badge, and identity behavior; OWNER offline kiosk scans sync as impersonated EMPLOYEE when auth is absent or fail when authenticated as OWNER due to actor mismatch.
required_correction: Fail closed when /api/attendance/* returns unexpected response; validate badges in direct fallback; store authenticated operator metadata safely or require live re-auth in offlineSync; enforce request.resource.data.get('employeeId', id) == id in attendance_status update.

title: Legacy Hardcoded Actor Fallbacks ('e1'/'e2'/'admin_sys') & Client Auto-Repair Side Effects
code_evidence: AttendanceLedger.tsx still writes userId: currentRole === 'OWNER' ? 'e1' : 'e2' in onAddForensicLog (lines 783, 872, 975; same in MassImportModal.tsx:608) and falls back to 'admin_sys' (772, 816, 860). AttendanceLedger.tsx:157-187 runs an uncontrolled useEffect auto-repair doing setDoc/deleteDoc on every mount with malformed dates. AttendanceLedger.tsx also duplicates processSecureScan instead of calling useQRScanner.
security_impact: Forensic log attribution is falsified to 'e1'/'e2' instead of real actor UID; any user opening AttendanceLedger triggers unrequested client deletes/rewrites; duplicate scanner logic risks drift.
required_correction: Replace all 'e1'/'e2'/'admin_sys' literals with resolved auth.currentUser?.uid; move date repair to a controlled admin migration script; consolidate duplicate QR scan handlers.

domain: RBAC Matrix Divergence Across Client Permission Modules
title: Client Permission Matrices Diverge on SUPERVISOR, HEAD_TELLER, and Teller Roles
code_evidence: 1) role.permissions.ts (hasPermission used by AttendanceLedger.tsx:743) completely omits HEAD_TELLER, SENIOR_TELLER, JUNIOR_TELLER, and AUDITOR, and sets SUPERVISOR.canOverrideAttendance = false. 2) PermissionRepository.getRolePermissions (repositories/index.ts:323, 339, 343) grants 'override_attendance' to SUPERVISOR, HEAD_TELLER, and MASTER_HEAD_TELLER, causing PermissionService.can('attendance.override') to return true (PermissionService.ts:976) even though ServerAttendanceService & AttendanceAuthorizationService deny overrides with 403 OVERRIDE_FORBIDDEN_FOR_ROLE. 3) PermissionRepository omits attendance.record_others from TEAM_LEADER while AttendanceAuthorizationService:711 grants TEAM_LEADER the same scope as SUPERVISOR.
security_impact: Inconsistent UI gating vs backend enforcement: SUPERVISOR and HEAD_TELLER see permission to override in PermissionService while server/rules reject it, and TEAM_LEADER diverges between authorization engine and permission matrix.
required_correction: Align ROLE_PERMISSIONS, PermissionRepository.defaultPermissionsMap, PermissionService, and AttendanceAuthorizationService to a single canonical capability matrix; remove override_attendance from SUPERVISOR/HEAD_TELLER and clarify TEAM_LEADER status.

title: Live Firestore Security Rules Execution Blocked & Integration Tests Rely on In-Memory Mocks
code_evidence: which java returned NO_JAVA in the verification environment. AttendanceP0RbacRemediation.test.ts uses vi.mock for firebaseAdmin, firebase/firestore, and lib/firebase backed by in-memory Maps, and verifies firestore.rules only via regex string matching (lines 950-992).
security_impact: Firestore security rules evaluation (including get/exists cross-doc lookups, null-safe resource checks, and negative client bypass tests) has NOT been executed against an actual Firestore Rules engine.
required_correction: Run @firebase/rules-unit-testing against local Firestore Emulator in a JDK-enabled CI/local environment covering all positive and negative matrix cases (including GAP-ATT-01 through GAP-ATT-04).
